newsitem.title: THAILAND: British minister hails Thai measures on finance.
newsitem.headline: British minister hails Thai measures on finance.

text.p: British Trade Minister Lord Clinton-Davis said on Wednesday he welcomed Thailand's decision to liberalise its financial sector.

Clinton-Davis, on a three-day visit to Thailand, told a news conference that he had discussed Thailand's plans to liberalise its financial sector with Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi earlier in the day.
The finance sector has been hit by a liquidity crunch and sour loans to the depressed property sector during the country's worst economic slump in a decade.
Clinton-Davis, who arrived in Bangkok on Tuesday, said Britain had expertise in this field and was willing to help Thailand overcome its economic problems.

His remarks followed four executive decrees issued by the Thai cabinet on Tuesday which allow greater foreign equity participation in new banks and the merging of finance companies as part of a bid to boost the financial sector.
Clinton-Davis said British investors believed there was a long-term future in Thailand and in Southeast Asia.
"I do believe that there are plenty of opportunities. We want to see Thai companies contributing even more to the business opportunities that are available inside Europe, inside Britain," he said.
